topic: software testing; Android GUI testing; LLM test oracles; multimodal evaluation
status: bounded candidate supported by one empirical Android study and a broader software-testing audit; not a novelty claim
claim: An LLM test oracle's practical value cannot be summarized by bug-detection rate alone. In one study of 71 curated Android non-crash bugs, GPT-4o's default integrated prompt correctly detected/described 49% of bugs but produced false alarms on 59% of bug-free sequences; a repeated-query setting raised TPC to 63% while false positives reached 93%. A separate app sweep surfaced 24 candidates across 64 apps, but only four were confirmed/fixed. The relevant deployment outcome is confirmed bugs per review cost, not alerts or candidate count.
positive_evidence: The Android study manually curated 71 reproducible bugs and defines TPC to require both bug identification and a correct description.
Default integrated setting: TPC 49%, false-positive rate 59%; single prompt: 42% TPC/29% FP; repeated integrated query: 63% TPC/93% FP.
The 64-app exploratory sweep reports 24 previously unrecognized candidates, four confirmed or fixed, directly separating candidate alerts from validated bugs.
The academic-search-engine study demonstrates that software testing can be grounded in replayable interactions and specific reproducible failures rather than relying only on broad claims.
counterevidence: The LLM result is on Android functional bugs and manually constructed/replayed sequences; it does not establish the same precision/recall tradeoff for other testing domains.
Only 71 of 399 candidate bugs were retained after manual review for reproducibility and bug-definition fit; the benchmark is carefully curated but not exhaustive.

The apparent advantage over specialized tools partly reflects broader semantic scope and different test-sequence requirements; the paper notes some comparators could not run the identical manually generated sequences.
The random software-testing cell also contains conceptual, instructional, and vision papers; these are not replications of the LLM-oracle result.

sources.sections: 71-bug curation; Table III and RQ1 discussion; separate 64-app discovery sweep
621 replicated search interactions, 42 engines, reproducible bug cases; study scope

falsifiable_test: Evaluate text-only, screenshot-only, and combined LLM oracles on independently held-out app families and curated functional bugs using identical replayable test sequences. Blindly adjudicate every alert. Report precision, recall, severity-weighted confirmed bugs per engineer-hour, run-to-run reproducibility, and confirmation rate for newly surfaced candidates. The practical-value hypothesis is weakened if added modalities or repeated queries fail to improve confirmed bugs per review-hour after false-alarm triage cost is counted, or if the apparent gain disappears on held-out apps.
limitations: Only one sampled empirical LLM-oracle paper; no independent replication in this audit. Discovery candidates are not confirmed bugs, and no effect sizes are pooled across the separate search-engine study. No novelty claim is made.
